_readme: Published list prices, per million tokens, USD. This file is a DATED SNAPSHOT of a
moving target: providers add, reprice, and retire models continuously. Every report
rendered from it states `as_of` and the share of calls it could actually price.
A model absent from `models` is NOT priced at zero. It is reported as unpriced: its
calls and tokens are counted, its dollars are omitted, and the report says so. Never
guess a rate to make a total look complete.
`rates` is a list of dated periods because prices change and a spend report prices
HISTORICAL calls. `from`/`to` are inclusive ISO dates; null means open-ended. When a
call carries no timestamp, the period covering `as_of` is used and the report labels
the figure as priced at current rates.
`ladder` names an intra-provider rung ordering (premium first, cheapest last) used only
for the price-differential ceiling. A null ladder means we have not reasoned about that
model's rungs and no ceiling is computed for it. Ladders never cross providers.
`aliases` maps an API model id ONTO an entry in `models`. It exists because a provider
response reports the id it actually served, which is not always the name a human types:
Anthropic's pre-4.6 generation answers with a dated snapshot (`claude-haiku-4-5` ->
`claude-haiku-4-5-20251001`), so a log captured straight from the API would otherwise
read as entirely unpriced. Every entry is TRANSCRIBED from the provider's own model
table, one line at a time -- there is no prefix matching, no date-stripping, and no
'looks like a Haiku' rule. An id we have not transcribed stays unpriced, which is the
honest answer; a guessed one would be a wrong dollar figure with our name on it.
Override with `kadari analyze --prices my-rates.json` if you hold negotiated pricing.
Corrections are welcome as pull requests; include the source URL and the date checked.

anthropic._note: Anthropic publishes cache rates as multiples of the input rate rather than as separate per-model figures.

_ladder_notes.gpt-5.5: gpt-5.5-mini and gpt-5.5-nano do not exist (verified 2026-08-05). The GPT-5.5 ladder's cheap rungs are the 5.4 generation, which is intra-provider and therefore in scope.

_omitted._why_this_block_exists: A model missing from `models` is normally just a model nobody has transcribed yet, and the readme above invites corrections as pull requests. That makes a DELIBERATE absence indistinguishable from an oversight — so the deliberate ones are recorded here with their reason, and re-adding one is a decision rather than a tidy-up.
_omitted.claude-mythos-5: Removed 2026-08-05 (founder call). Invitation-only within Project Glasswing, and offered for defensive cybersecurity work — a high-stakes vertical that ADR-0001 puts out of scope. Anyone with access to it is not the naive-heavy-spender ICP this table serves, and listing it in a public price table implies we price and reason about traffic we have deliberately not entered. A holder who runs the tool anyway sees those calls reported as UNPRICED — counted, dollars omitted, share stated — which is the correct answer for a model we do not serve, not a failure.
_omitted.claude-mythos-preview: Never listed. Same programme; and its pricing is not published, so listing it would require a guess.
_omitted.bedrock_and_vertex_ids: See `_alias_notes.cloud_resellers` — those platforms publish their own rates, so pricing that traffic from this table would be a number the customer cannot reconcile against their invoice.

_alias_notes._source: Anthropic entries transcribed from the 'Claude API ID' / 'Claude API alias' rows of the models overview (checked 2026-08-05); `gpt-5.6` -> `gpt-5.6-sol` from OpenAI's models page (checked 2026-08-05).
_alias_notes.anthropic: Only the pre-4.6 generation carries a dated id. From Claude 4.6 onward the API ID is dateless and identical to the alias (claude-opus-5, claude-sonnet-5, claude-sonnet-4-6, ...), so those need no alias entry -- they are already table keys.
_alias_notes.openai_dated_snapshots: OpenAI dated snapshots are deliberately NOT aliased. Its pricing page prices them independently -- `gpt-4o` is $2.50/$10 while `gpt-4o-2024-05-13` is $5.00/$15.00 -- so folding a snapshot onto its base name would halve a real bill. A snapshot we hold a published rate for is listed in `models` with its own rate; one we do not is reported unpriced.
_alias_notes.cloud_resellers: Bedrock (`anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-5-20250929-v1:0`) and Vertex (`claude-sonnet-4-5@20250929`) ids are NOT aliased either: those platforms publish their own pricing, so charging that traffic at Claude API rates would be a number the customer cannot reconcile against their invoice.

gpt-4o-2024-05-13.note: Priced separately from `gpt-4o` by OpenAI ($5/$15 vs $2.50/$10) -- which is why an OpenAI dated snapshot is never aliased onto its base name.
